svg.title: Motion law of the 180° APC turn (example)
svg.text: Motion law for the 180° turn in 2.5 s – trapezoid 30 % (page) vs modified sine vs cycloidal
J = 338 kg·m² (both pallets loaded) · T = J·α + 10 N·m friction · r = 0.48 m. Curves computed with Python (scratch g09/calc.py).
θ(x) normalised, x = t/T, h = π rad
ω max = Cv·h/T, α max = Ca·h/T² (units rad/s, rad/s²)
Jerk: trapezoid ∞ (steps in α) · mod. sine 69.5·h/T³
Motor (i 200, η 0.9): mod. sine 5.28 N·m at 4 223 rpm
→ 2.0 kW servo needs 7.1 of 19 N·m, n ≤ 5 000 ✓
Cycloidal: 4 800 rpm – near the 5 000 rpm limit
Pallet on rails at the end of accel.: mod. sine
Same accel. torque as trapezoid (810 N·m): mod. sine
needs T = 2.69 s instead of 2.5 s (+0.19 s)
Electronic cam in the servo drive or cam indexer.
Digital twin · values: web/apc.js defaults, guide 25 §14
